The main takeaway from our work is that
creoles were the dominant force in the administration of Spanish America by the 1770S.

the Spanish crown's efforts to improve the administration of justice in America during the eighteenthcentury led to a dramatic increase in the number of creoles appointed to the audiencias of New Spain, Peru, and Chile, and that the creole judges, once appointed, tended to stay in office for long terms of office, sometimes even for life.
creoles, especially those born and educated in their home cities, were not excluded from government, as many historians have assumed, but were in fact the most numerous group in the audiencias.
